stem:
A 60-year-old man's blood pressure is measured as 140/90 mm Hg during a routine clinic examination. He has no symptoms and his heart rate is regular.

Which of the following values is closest to his mean arterial pressure?

options.label: A
options.misconception: The diastolic pressure alone is being reported as the mean.
options.explanation: Mean pressure adds one-third of the pulse pressure to diastolic pressure; diastolic alone underestimates the time-averaged pressure.

options.label: B
options.misconception: The arithmetic midpoint of systolic and diastolic is being used.
options.explanation: Because diastole lasts longer than systole, mean pressure is weighted toward diastolic (one-third of pulse pressure above it), not the 115 mm Hg midpoint.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; diastolic plus one-third of the pulse pressure gives 90 + 50/3 ≈ 107 mm Hg.
options.explanation: Mean arterial pressure equals diastolic pressure plus one-third of the difference between systolic and diastolic pressures: 90 + (140-90)/3 ≈ 107 mm Hg.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Two-thirds rather than one-third of the pulse pressure is being added.
options.explanation: Adding two-thirds of the pulse pressure overweights systole; the correct weighting gives about 107 mm Hg.

options.label: E
options.misconception: The systolic peak is being reported as the mean.
options.explanation: Systolic pressure is the maximum, not the time-averaged, pressure; the mean is much closer to the diastolic value.

context: Learning objective: compute mean arterial pressure. MAP equals diastolic pressure plus one-third of the pulse pressure (systolic minus diastolic).
imageCaption: Poiseuille r^4, MAP, venous capacitance, Starling edema, coronary origins.
